MMWR Week 40: September 29 - October 05, 2024 (Season 2024-2025) — reporting year 2024
Source: Virginia Department of Health (VDH), Respiratory Disease Program
URL: https://www.vdh.virginia.gov/content/uploads/sites/3/2024/10/Weekly-RDS-Report_Week-40.pdf

Note: Generated from VDH's Weekly Respiratory Disease Surveillance Report PDF

reproduced from the report. Sections 1-3 are ~150-word summaries that
incorporate the table and figure information within each section.


## At a Glance

During the week of September 29 - October 05, 2024 (MMWR Week 40), Virginia
reported 12.4% of ED visits were for respiratory illnesses. This is a 0.1 point
decrease from the previous week. For the 2024-25 season, 0 pediatric deaths
associated with influenza have been reported in Virginia. More data and details
on flu surveillance can be found here.

  - ED and urgent care visits for diagnosed acute respiratory illness remained
    stable, visits for Influenza Like Illness (ILI) remained stable, visits for
    diagnosed COVID-19 decreased 26%, visits for diagnosed Influenza increased
    6%, and visits for diagnosed Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) remained low
    compared to the previous week. None of them were significantly elevated in
    Virginia's syndromic surveillance system compared to a baseline of previous
    weeks.
  - 7 respiratory outbreaks (1 confirmed, 5 suspected, 1 unknown) were reported
    this week; a 30% decrease from the previous week. The etiologic agent for
    most of the outbreaks (5; 71%) was SARS-CoV-2.
  - 49 confirmatory influenza labs were received this week, a 48% increase from
    the previous week.


## 1. Syndromic Surveillance — Summary (~150 words)

Drawing on emergency department and urgent care visit data, the section's five
trend figures show low, early-season respiratory activity in Week 40, with no
measure significantly elevated above baseline. Diagnosed acute respiratory
illness remained stable, edging from 19.2% to 19.4% of visits. Influenza-like
illness also remained stable, moving from 2.4% to 2.6% of visits. Diagnosed
COVID-19 visits decreased 26%, from 1,904 to 1,404, the largest proportional
move, but were not elevated. Diagnosed influenza visits increased 6%, from 321 to
341, a modest early-season rise that was not elevated. RSV visits remained low
(under 50 statewide), rising from 25 to 36 visits. Across the figures, no red or
yellow alert markers were triggered, with all five indicators sitting within
expected baseline ranges—indicating quiet early-fall respiratory circulation
across Virginia for the week ending October 5, 2024, as the new season began.


## 2. Outbreak Surveillance — Summary (~150 words)

A total of 7 respiratory outbreaks were reported (1 confirmed, 5 suspected, 1
unknown), a 30% decrease from the prior week. By etiologic agent, SARS-CoV-2
dominated with 5 outbreaks, followed by 1 Enterovirus/Rhinovirus and 1 of unknown
agent. Table 1 distributes outbreaks by region and etiologic agent: Central
reported 1 Enterovirus/Rhinovirus and 1 unknown; Northwest reported 2 SARS-CoV-2;
and Southwest reported 3 SARS-CoV-2. The weekly trend graphs cover October 2023
through October 2024. The influenza outbreak graph notes that for the 2024-25
season, 0 influenza outbreaks have been reported—consistent with the early-season
timing. SARS-CoV-2 remained the leading driver of facility-based transmission,
concentrated in the Southwest and Northwest regions, while no influenza outbreaks
had yet been recorded for the new season. Overall outbreak activity was low and
declining for the week ending October 5, 2024.


## 3. Laboratory Surveillance — Summary (~150 words)

VDH received a total of 49 positive confirmatory influenza labs this week that
were able to be subtyped, a 48% increase from the previous week. Of those, most
(47; 96%) were Flu A and 2 were Flu B. Since the start of the 2024-25 flu season
(week ending October 5, 2024), VDH received a total of 49 positive influenza
labs. Per Table 2, the season subtype breakdown comprises 2 Flu A (H1), 1 Flu A
(H3), and 2 Flu B, with 44 Flu A labs without subtyping reported either because
subtyping was not performed or there was insufficient specimen. By region (Table
3), all 49 labs came from the 5 health planning regions, with most (42; 86%)
reported from the Eastern, Northern, and Central regions. Because only
confirmatory PCR, culture, and DFA results are reportable—rapid antigen tests are
excluded—these counts represent a small fraction of all influenza infections but
reliably indicate circulating strains as the season begins.
